mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or authorized Commissioner for Oaths in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents, in force for Canada effective 11 January 2024); apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada or Ontario Official Documents Services

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days) for each 25%+ UBO and General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in the residence country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostilled (Hague Apostille) if issued by a public utility or public authority; privately issued bank statements accepted with notarized signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance for any corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the General Partner's incorporating jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency for corporate General Partner listing directors, officers, and signing authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank of the General Partner or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization not required in Canada; notarized signature accepted by Canadian counsel and financial institutions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all General Partners, 25%+ UBOs, and authorized signatories against (1) FINTRAC/OSFI advisories; (2) UN Security Council sanctions implemented through the United Nations Act; (3) Special Economic Measures Act listings; (4) Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act sanctions; (5) Criminal Code Schedule VI terrorist entity listings; (6) OFAC SDN List, which is mandatory because Apple App Store and Google Play payouts settle in USD through US financial infrastructure. Enhanced due diligence, including verified source-of-funds documentation and senior-management approval, applies to any foreign or domestic PEP, head of state, judge, or senior public official and their family members/close associates per FINTRAC PEP guidance. The LP is classified as Low_Risk_Standard (non-MS B) under PCMLTFA for software publishing, but its banking and payout partners will apply independent FATF-aligned KYC. Non-resident ownership is permitted without restriction; however, non-resident UBOs trigger enhanced FATF cross-border scrutiny and US withholding considerations on effectively connected income.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry operated by ServiceOntario (businessregistry.ontario.ca) under the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All registered names must use the Latin alphabet (English and/or French). Non-Latin scripts are prohibited in the statutory name, but transliteration for trade-mark and domain reference is permitted in supplementary documentation. The legal element must be appended: 'Limited Partnership', 'LP', or 'L.P.' in English, or 'Société en commandite' in French. A mandatory Ontario NUANS Name Search Report must accompany the Declaration of Limited Partnership to prove the name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to any active corporate, LP, trademark, or registered business name in Canada.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Inc./Corporation/Incorporée (implies a corporation; prohibited for a limited partnership)
Bank/Banque/Trust/Insurance/Assurance (requires OSFI prior approval under federal financial regulatory statutes)
University/College/Institute (requires ministry consent or accreditation evidence)
Royal/Crown/Canada/Government (implies Crown or official sponsorship, requires ministerial consent)
Charitable/Foundation/Fund (implies registered charity status, requires approval)
War/Genocide/Obscene or scandalous expressions contrary to public policy (administrative discretion to refuse)
Words creating confusion with a federal or provincial court, tribunal, or government program
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The NUANS report is valid for 90 days from the date of issue; no statutory extension exists, and a new search report (CAD 13.80) must be obtained after expiry. Upon name refusal, the applicant shall: (1) Refile a fresh NUANS search with a revised distinctive element and resubmit the Declaration of Limited Partnership; (2) Submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of the Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, within 30 days of the refusal, attaching the NUANS report, proposed name, and written legal submissions distinguishing the proposed name from cited conflicting marks; (3) If the Director upholds the refusal, the applicant has 30 days from the final decision to apply for judicial review to the Ontario Divisional Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSO 1990, c. J.1. Legal counsel should evaluate risks of passing-off and trademark infringement before pursuing appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted. Section 6 of the Limited Partnerships Act, RSO 1990, c. L.16 requires a registered office with a physical street address in Ontario for service of process; ServiceOntario accepts a commercial virtual-office suite address. However, Apple App Store and Google Play payout onboarding requires a verifiable physical business address and an active D-U-N-S number; Canadian banks may refuse an operating account for an LP lacking physical substance. If the LP later processes player payments directly (rather than through Apple/Google rails) and becomes a money-services business under PCMLTFA, section 11.2 of PCMLTFA mandates an actual physical office. Virtual office alone satisfies incorporation mechanics but is insufficient for payment-rail and banking commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% - Low. ISIC 5820 (software publishing / MMORPG) is not a regulated non-financial entity under PCMLTFA unless the LP itself conducts money transmission or becomes a PSP. CRA audits are documentary in nature; FINTRAC does not conduct inspections of non-MSB entities; unannounced visits are only realistic if the LP expands into prohibited or regulated activities. The higher practical risk is contract-driven inspection: Apple/Google compliance interviews may request evidence of the declared office, and the expected service provider should maintain a directory listing and mail-handling trail.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.7, ss. 2, 3, 5, 9 and 11; Business Names Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.17; General Regulation R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 690
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (ServiceOntario)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Declaration of Limited Partnership under the Limited Partnerships Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Ontario Limited Partnership. Capital contributions are determined by the partnership agreement and may, if stipulated by the agreement, be held in escrow until the partnership is registered and operating.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED by the General Partner of the Limited Partnership: 1. The subscription of all Limited Partnership units and the admission and capital contributions of the Limited Partners as set out in the Subscription Schedule are accepted, effective upon filing of the Declaration. 2. The registered office shall be located at the address provided with the Declaration in the Province of Ontario, and the General Partner is authorized to maintain statutory records at that office. 3. The General Partner appoints [name] as managing officer, with authority to execute registrations, open banking accounts, engage accountants/tax counsel, and effect all filings under the Limited Partnerships Act and Business Names Act. 4. All partners are authorized to take all further action necessary to perfect formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ontario LP Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a precedence search for the proposed LP name through a licensed Name Search provider or ONBIS. The name report must show no identical or confusingly similar business, LP, or corporate names. Submit name reservation if the platform offers it; otherwise preserve the name report for filing. If the name is unavailable, select a revised name and repeat the search.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, obtain a revised Name Search Report with a new proposed name and resubmit within the service-level period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (via legal counsel or authorized agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 — Declaration of Limited Partnership under the Limited Partnerships Act, setting out the firm name, registered office, names and addresses of general partners and limited partners, contribution amounts, term, and authorized business. The general partner(s) must execute the Declaration before filing. A certificate of acknowledgment may be required for notarization of non-resident general partners.
required_dossiers: Identification and proof of standing for any corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Prior to submission, any inadequacy is cured by amending the draft and obtaining fresh signatures; legal counsel will issue a corrected Declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration with Ontario Ministry and Pay Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (ServiceOntario)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration and required fee electronically via ServiceOntario's online registration portal, or in person at a ServiceOntario service center. Upon acceptance, the Ministry issues a stamped or endorsed copy confirming the LP is registered. Retain the endorsed copy for tax and bank account purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query is issued, respond through ServiceOntario within 30 days with an amended Declaration or a verifying explanation; refiling without penalty for ministerial error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain CRA Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LP online through the CRA Business Registration Online service using the endorsed Declaration. Obtain the 9-digit Business Number and select required program accounts: GST/HST, payroll, or other applicable tax accounts. The LP is generally a pass-through entity for Canadian tax purposes; determine partnership-level GST/HST obligations and any Ontario EHT or WSIB requirements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the application due to identity mismatch, verify with the Ontario registry and resubmit the corrected BN request online; expedited telephone support is available for urgent matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Municipal and Occupational Premises Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Toronto Municipal Licensing & Standards or local municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the physical registered office if placing office premises in Ontario; obtain an occupancy permit or zoning confirmation. For a pure MMORPG publishing operation, this step generally requires a Business Premises Occupancy Permit. If the LP operates a physical server presence, submit electrical and fire safety inspection reports.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal licensing flags non-compliance, remediate fire or zoning deficiencies and attach the certificate of correction; request re-inspection within 14 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Licensing & Standards, City of Toronto; Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA) for any regulated equipment; no sectoral industrial licensing board applies to MMORPG software publishing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business / Premises Occupancy Permit (no sector-specific operating license required for MMORPG software publishing activity)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category C — non-manufacturing office/software activity; no mandatory EIA screening requirement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge threshold applicable. General duty under Environmental Protection Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.19 not to cause adverse effects; waste handling per O. Reg. 347; electrical/electronic equipment recycling compliance under the Ontario Electronics Stewardship Program if server hardware is used.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07); structural load acceptance per landlord's building occupancy certificate; workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1, including WSIB registration if employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - GST/HST and Business Number registration through the CRA's GST/HST Registry portal; Ontario Ministry of Finance for provincial tax matters.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership must determine whether it is carrying on business in Canada. If yes, apply for a CRA Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST program account using Form RC1 or through CRA's online services. The partnership must provide its name, address, country of residence, list of Canadian partners (if any), and describe its taxable activities. If the partnership has no permanent establishment in Canada but is required to register, CRA will issue a BN with a 'RT' program account. Ontario registration (e.g., Employer Health Tax, withholdings) may be required if employees are present. There is no separate corporate tax identification for an Ontario limited partnership; each partner reports income under their own tax system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible for Canadian income tax purposes (the partnership is not a taxable entity; partners declare their share). For GST/HST purposes, the partnership itself is a separate 'person' and must register if taxable supplies exceed the threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available for a Canadian limited partnership under federal income tax law. For GST/HST, partnerships may elect to use the Simplified Accounting Method or make a section 221 election regarding filing frequency. For hybrid mismatch avoidance, Canada has rules that can deny deductions for carved-out payments, but these are not elective. The partnership's fiscal year must conform to Canadian tax rules unless a CRA election is made with the consent of all partners.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Ontario applies a single HST combining federal and provincial components.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in any four consecutive calendar quarters. For non-resident suppliers of digital services to Canadian consumers, the same threshold applies; mandatory registration arises once the threshold is surpassed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime exists in Canada. Electronic invoices are accepted provided they are accurate, legible, and retained. CRA does not operate a pre-clearance API system for invoices, but electronic records must be kept in a secure, retrievable format (preferably in Canada or accessible to CRA on demand). Ontario has no separate e-invoicing clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of an MMORPG digital service is zero-rated under Part V of Schedule IX to the Excise Tax Act when supplied to a non-resident recipient and the recipient is not registered for GST/HST, and the use of the intellectual property is not for consumption in Canada. Digital gaming services distributed through Apple App Store / Google Play to end users outside Canada qualify for zero-rating if evidence shows the customer is non-resident and the download occurs outside Canada. Supplies made to Canadian residents are subject to 13% HST at the point of sale.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (not applicable to pure digital services; no physical goods movement)
Commercial invoice or itemized in-app purchase transaction log from the mobile platform
Apple App Store / Google Play payout statements showing gross sales by territory and non-resident origin
Inward Remittance Certificate / banking records proving receipt of FX funds from foreign platform marketplaces
Geo-location and IP address evidence, plus recipient non-resident status documentation
License agreement or terms of service indicating the service is supplied for use outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated supplies within four years (unlimited if misrepresentation or fraud). Improper zero-rating results in immediate reassessment of 13% HST payable, interest, and penalties. Gross negligence penalties under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act can equal up to 25% of the net tax understated; intentional misconduct may also trigger third-party penalties and prosecution. The partnership and its general partner may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid GST/HST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — Canada's central bank and monetary authority. Banking prudential supervision rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/ATF supervision rests with FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada). Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange-control administration (no SAFE-equivalent); residual currency powers sit with the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of the Canadian dollar (CAD) on both current and capital account under Canada's IMF Article VIII obligations. There are zero exchange controls, no prior approvals, and no ceilings on profit or distribution remittance by non-resident limited partners of an Ontario LP. Remittance exposure is limited to Part XIII withholding tax (default 25%, treaty-reduced where applicable) and to Investment Canada Act review only for controlling acquisitions of Canadian businesses — neither applies to passive LP capital contributions or profit distributions. The CAD floats freely; foreign-currency (USD/EUR) bank accounts may be opened without regulatory consent, and treasury managers may net or convert freely at market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no surrender requirement, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts. All proceeds from global MMORPG in-app purchases (Apple App Store and Google Play payouts) may be retained in USD or any deliverable currency indefinitely. Statutory reporting is limited to: the T5013 Partnership Information Return; Form T1135 (Foreign Income Verification Statement) where specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000; and FINTRAC large-currency/EFT transaction reports (CAD 10,000 threshold) filed by the financial intermediary.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility — legally constrained. Canada does not issue EU-style EMI licences; a foreign digital bank or EMI must register as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and appoint a Canadian agent for service before lawfully holding funds for an Ontario LP. Offshore EMIs without FINTRAC registration cannot accept deposits from Canadian-resident entities. Platforms such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Stripe operate FINTRAC-registered MSB models and can support payout receivables and operational FX, but none provides institutional escrow-grade counterparty capacity. Recommended architecture: all capital-escrow and treasury functions held at a Schedule I bank; FINTRAC-registered MSBs may receive Apple/Google small-value payouts only where the flow is swept daily to the Schedule I primary bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally available for an Ontario LP at Schedule I banks via video-verified KYC, provided the general partner delivers certified corporate documents, the Ontario Declaration of Limited Partnership, and completes a live compliance interview. No statute mandates physical in-branch attendance; however, banks may require an in-person meeting where (i) the general partner is incorporated in a high-risk jurisdiction, (ii) any limited partner is non-resident beyond FATF-reviewed countries, or (iii) directors lack machine-readable identity records. Efficiency tactic: appoint a Canadian-resident authorized signatory and pre-submit the FINTRAC beneficial-ownership register (identifying every 25%+ owner) to avoid physical-presence conditions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners holding 25% or more of the LP (FINTRAC beneficial-ownership look-through under the PCMLTFA and its revised ownership-determination rules).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete LP register with corporate organogram; certified KYC pack per 25%+ limited partner (government-issued photo ID, proof of address, 12-month source-of-funds bank statements); signed PCMLTFA beneficial-ownership attestation; capital-commitment letters; Ontario counsel legal opinion confirming the ownership chain and absence of nominees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore or corporate general partner with no demonstrated substance in Ontario (perceived 'shell' or conduit risk).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Declaration of Limited Partnership and annual filings; GP board resolutions authorizing banking; notarized GP certificate of existence; GP director CVs and background checks; registered-office lease and utility evidence; FATCA/CRS registration copies; documentary proof of T5013/T2 compliance history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency small-value Apple/Google payout inflows flagged as unusual digital-revenue patterns without underlying commercial documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console payout agreements; payout configuration dashboards (currency, frequency); 12-month earnings statements; representative player transaction audit trail; reconciliations mapping App Store Connect/Play Console remittances to bank credits; ISIC 5820 business narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity-class mismatch — LP documents describe a passive investment pool but the banking application requests active treasury operations (FINTRAC consistent-usage suspicion).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: If active: amended LP Agreement expressly permitting software publishing and treasury hedging; board minutes; operational cash-flow forecast. If passive: capital-escrow-only mandate with segregated accounts, disclaimers of active trading, and a distribution policy memo; compliance with the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act 'carrying on business' determination.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for cover) from each limited partner's bank to the LP's segregated account at the chosen Schedule I bank; the beneficiary reference field must carry the LP's Ontario Declaration number, full legal name, and 'Capital Contribution' narrative. Canada has no government-mandated purpose-code list; banks map the narrative internally to ISO 20022 purpose codes (e.g., EQTY or CFSR). The GP must pre-file a capital-call resolution, and the contribution must reconcile with the LP Agreement's schedule. FINTRAC EFT reporting applies at CAD 10,000. For USD capital originating from Apple/Google treasury operations, funds route via Fedwire to the LP's USD account at the bank's US clearing correspondent; CAD conversion, if desired, is executed at prevailing spot with no regulatory approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border disbursements; (2) Lynx — Payments Canada's high-value payment system — for final, irrevocable CAD settlement in Bank of Canada central-bank money; (3) ACSS/EFT for low-value domestic payments. MMORPG revenue flows from Apple/Google as USD wires or ACH to the LP's USD account; treasury sweeps USD to CAD via intraday FX at the primary bank. Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) are permissible but non-essential for digital licensing; they may be used if the LP procures physical hardware or localized content from overseas vendors. Standard Settlement Instructions (SSIs) must be verified by second-channel confirmation before high-value execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD) — vanilla instruments, executed under ISDA 1998/2002 master agreements; no regulatory pre-approval
FX options and zero-cost collars (CAD/USD) — permissible treasury instruments for revenue-share smoothing
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CAD/USD) — available from Schedule I banks; requires clear treasury mandate and board approval
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — legally permissible but redundant for CAD; used only for exotic/EM currency exposures
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) — permitted for liquidity rebalancing across CAD, USD, and EUR accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ServiceOntario (Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Province of Ontario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date of the partnership's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee imposed; persistent non-filing may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution under the Limited Partnerships Act (Ontario).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the fifth month following the end of the partnership's fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under the Income Tax Act, including a minimum penalty of $100 and additional amounts for repeated failure; wilful default may lead to criminal prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act or the Canada Income Tax Act for a limited partnership. An independent audit may become required by the partnership agreement, a lender, or securities regulations if the LP is a reporting issuer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for reporting issuers; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS for private partnerships. Books and records must satisfy CRA record-keeping requirements under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario Limited Partnerships are not subject to an annual UBO confirmation filing. However, changes in partners must be submitted to ServiceOntario by filing a Declaration of Change within 30 days. Beneficial ownership information must be maintained internally for CRA and anti-money laundering compliance where applicable.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal (15% general) and Ontario (11.5% general) corporate rates; the Ontario Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent and tax is borne by its partners at their respective rates
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No MMORPG-specific statutory holiday; available incentives include the federal SR&ED investment tax credit (35% refundable for qualifying CCPC expenditures up to the annual expenditure limit) and the Ontario Innovation Tax Credit, plus the federal small business deduction (9%) and Ontario small business deduction (3.2%) on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income allocated to an eligible corporate partner
